generatedFrom: SY0-701 official exam objectives domain weights + public high-yield study consensus (2024–2025). Explicitly excludes NDA-protected live items / braindumps.
disclaimer: These mid-review packs estimate “most likely to matter” topics using public blueprint weights and common prep patterns. They are not reconstructed CompTIA exam questions and are not affiliated with CompTIA.

cards.title: IR lifecycle order
cards.secret: Preparation → Detection/Analysis → Containment/Eradication/Recovery → Lessons learned. Never skip contain before eradicate on live threats.
cards.trap: Jumping straight to eradication or “lessons learned first.”

cards.title: Contain before eradicate
cards.secret: If malware is spreading, isolate/contain first. Eradicate after blast radius is limited.
cards.trap: Reimaging every host before isolation (spreads further / loses evidence).

cards.title: Chain of custody
cards.secret: Document who handled evidence, when, and how. Required for legal/forensic integrity.
cards.trap: Copying evidence casually without logs “to save time.”

cards.title: MFA beats passwords alone
cards.secret: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) > SMS OTP > password-only. Scenario asking best identity control → MFA/PAM.
cards.trap: Longer passwords alone as the “best” fix for remote compromise risk.

cards.title: Least privilege / JIT
cards.secret: Standing Domain Admin is almost never the answer. Prefer JIT elevation + PAM vault + just-enough rights.

cards.title: SIEM job
cards.secret: Centralize logs → correlate → alert. SIEM ≠ EDR ≠ SOAR (SOAR automates response playbooks).

cards.title: EDR vs antivirus
cards.secret: EDR = detect/investigate/respond on endpoints with behavioral telemetry; AV alone is signature-limited.

cards.title: Credentialed scans
cards.secret: Authenticated scans find missing patches more accurately than unauthenticated.
cards.trap: Assuming external port scan equals full vuln coverage.

cards.title: Attack surface reduction
cards.secret: Disable unused services, close ports, secure baselines/gold images, host firewalls.
cards.trap: Only adding more tools without removing exposure.

cards.title: Full disk encryption
cards.secret: Protects data-at-rest if laptop is lost/stolen while locked/off. Not a fix for phishing.
cards.trap: Using FDE as answer for in-transit eavesdropping.

cards.title: Conditional access
cards.secret: Require MFA/compliant device based on risk, location, app. Context-aware identity control.
cards.trap: Static allow-all from “trusted network” (breaks zero trust).

cards.title: Playbooks / SOAR
cards.secret: Playbook = predefined IR steps; SOAR executes/orchestrates them with integrations.
cards.trap: Confusing playbook with BIA or risk register.

cards.title: IoC vs IoA
cards.secret: IoC = forensic artifact of compromise (hash, IP). Hunting often looks for behaviors (IoA) too.
cards.trap: Treating every IoC as proof without context.

cards.title: Tabletop vs walkthrough
cards.secret: Tabletop = discussion/decision drill. Functional/full-interrupt tests exercise live systems.
cards.trap: Calling a live failover a tabletop.

cards.title: Phishing family
cards.secret: Phishing=broad email; spear=targeted; whaling=exec; vishing=voice; smishing=SMS; BEC=fraudulent wire via email.

cards.title: Ransomware impact
cards.secret: Hits integrity + availability. Best mitigations: immutable/offline backups + segmentation + least privilege.
cards.trap: Paying ransom as the security control.

cards.title: Injection / SQLi
cards.secret: Unvalidated input → SQLi/XSS. Fix: parameterized queries/ORM + input validation + WAF as layer.

cards.title: XSS
cards.secret: Injects script into victim browser/session. Output encoding + CSP. Different from CSRF.
cards.trap: Calling XSS a server-side SQL problem.

cards.title: Pass-the-hash
cards.secret: Reuse NTLM hash to authenticate without cracking. Mitigate: Credential Guard, LAPS, restrict admin logons, PAM.

cards.title: DoS / DDoS
cards.secret: Availability attack. Mitigate with scrubbing/CDN/rate limits — not antivirus.

cards.title: Threat actors
cards.secret: Nation-state=espionage/persistence; hacktivist=ideology; insider=privilege abuse; script kiddie=kits; shadow IT=unsanctioned tools.

cards.title: Supply chain / watering hole
cards.secret: Compromise vendor/update or sites victims visit. Mitigate: vendor risk, code signing, allowlisting.

cards.title: EOL / unpatched
cards.secret: No more vendor patches = critical risk. Isolate, upgrade, or compensate.

cards.title: Allowlisting
cards.secret: Best against unknown ransomware executables when paired with least privilege.
cards.trap: Relying only on denylist AV signatures.

cards.title: ARP spoof / on-path
cards.secret: L2 MITM on local segment. Mitigate: dynamic ARP inspection, 802.1X, encryption.

cards.title: Risk treatment 4
cards.secret: Mitigate / Transfer (insurance) / Avoid (cancel) / Accept (documented approval).

cards.title: ALE = SLE × ARO
cards.secret: Quantitative classic. Compare ALE to control cost.

cards.title: Inherent vs residual
cards.secret: Inherent = before controls; residual = after. Acceptance is about residual.

cards.title: BIA
cards.secret: Identifies critical processes and impact of disruption → drives RTO/RPO priorities.
cards.trap: Thinking BIA is a pen test report.

cards.title: RTO vs RPO
cards.secret: RTO=time to restore service; RPO=how much data loss (time) is tolerable.

cards.title: Separation of duties
cards.secret: No single person owns end-to-end critical process (e.g., request + approve + pay).
cards.trap: Job rotation as the same thing (related but different).

cards.title: PCI vs GDPR vs HIPAA
cards.secret: PCI=cardholder data; GDPR=EU personal data; HIPAA=US health PHI.
cards.trap: Applying PCI to all PII scenarios.

cards.title: Third-party risk
cards.secret: Assess vendors, contracts, right-to-audit, data handling SLAs.
cards.trap: Trusting SOC logo without scope review.

cards.title: Policy types
cards.secret: AUP=acceptable use; policy=high-level; standard=mandatory specifics; procedure=how-to; guideline=recommended.

cards.title: Awareness metrics
cards.secret: Measure behavior change (phishing sim click rates), not just attendance.
cards.trap: Certificate of attendance as proof of effectiveness.

cards.title: Zero Trust
cards.secret: Never trust by network location. Verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach.

cards.title: Defense in depth
cards.secret: Layer complementary controls so one failure isn’t catastrophic.
cards.trap: Single perfect firewall as complete answer.

cards.title: Segmentation / microseg
cards.secret: Limits east-west lateral movement. Critical for ransomware and OT isolation.

cards.title: DMZ / screened subnet
cards.secret: Public services live in DMZ with controlled paths to internal.

cards.title: WAF placement
cards.secret: In front of web apps for HTTP exploits (SQLi/XSS). Complements, doesn’t replace secure code.
cards.trap: WAF instead of network firewall for all traffic types.

cards.title: Data states
cards.secret: At rest→encrypt disks/DB; in transit→TLS/IPsec; in use→hardest (confidential computing / access control).
cards.trap: One control covering all three states.

cards.title: Tokenization vs encryption
cards.secret: Tokenization replaces value with vault-mapped token; encryption transforms with key math.

cards.title: Hot / warm / cold site
cards.secret: Hot≈ready failover; warm=partial; cold=facility only. Cost ↔ RTO tradeoff.

cards.title: Cloud shared responsibility
cards.secret: Provider secures cloud; you secure in-cloud (IAM, data, configs). SaaS vs IaaS shifts the line.
cards.trap: Assuming provider patches your guest OS in IaaS.

cards.title: IaC security
cards.secret: Versioned, reviewable, repeatable infra reduces drift — scan templates for misconfig.
cards.trap: Manual snowflake servers as more secure.

cards.title: Control types
cards.secret: Managerial=policy/risk; Technical=firewall/MFA; Operational=processes/reviews; Physical=locks/guards. Also preventive/detective/corrective/deterrent/compensating/directive.

cards.title: CIA + non-repudiation
cards.secret: Confidentiality=secrecy; Integrity=unaltered; Availability=usable; Non-repudiation=can’t deny (signatures).

cards.title: Hash vs encrypt
cards.secret: Hash=one-way integrity; Encrypt=reversible confidentiality (with key); Sign=auth+integrity.

cards.title: Symmetric vs asymmetric
cards.secret: AES=fast shared key; RSA/ECC=public/private for exchange/signatures. Hybrid TLS uses both.

cards.title: PKI basics
cards.secret: CA signs certs; Issuer=CA; SAN=hostnames; revoke via CRL/OCSP. Compromised CA = trust crisis.
cards.trap: Self-signed as equal to public CA trust for browsers.

cards.title: AAA
cards.secret: Authentication=who; Authorization=what allowed; Accounting=what happened (logs).

cards.title: Deception
cards.secret: Honeypot/honeytoken detects/observes attackers — not production storage.

cards.title: Change management
cards.secret: Approve, document, rollback plan. Untracked change = outage + audit fail.
cards.trap: Emergency change with zero records forever.

cards.title: PBQ time strategy
cards.secret: Flag PBQs early, crush MCQs, return with remaining time. Simulations are skippable with work saved.

cards.title: Firewall PBQ logic
cards.secret: Top-down first match. Specific allows before broad deny. Explicit deny at end for host.

cards.title: Log triage PBQ
cards.secret: Look for Office→PowerShell, encoded commands, rare outbound C2, unsigned downloads. Ignore toner/normal TGT.

cards.title: Matching PBQs
cards.secret: Map example→control type or risk treatment using definitions, not vibes.

cards.title: “BEST / MOST” wording
cards.secret: Pick the control that most directly reduces the stated risk with least side effects. Prefer preventive when prevention is possible.

cards.title: BEC
cards.secret: Business Email Compromise = social engineering for wire fraud/gift cards via spoofed exec mail. Train finance + out-of-band verify.

cards.title: Credential stuffing
cards.secret: Replayed breach passwords across sites. Mitigate: MFA + breach monitoring + blocklists + no reuse.
cards.trap: Only forcing weekly password change without MFA.

cards.title: Buffer overflow
cards.secret: Missing bounds checks → memory overwrite / code exec. Mitigate: patch, ASLR/DEP, secure coding.

cards.title: Logic bomb
cards.secret: Triggers on date/condition. Often insider-planted. Audit + least privilege + code review.
cards.trap: Confusing with ransomware encryption stage alone.

cards.title: Shadow IT
cards.secret: Unsanctioned SaaS bypasses logging/SSO/DLP. Discover + CASB/SSPM + approved catalog.
cards.trap: Blocking without offering alternatives (drives more shadow).

cards.title: OT / ICS isolation
cards.secret: Segment OT from IT; strict change control; avoid casual Internet on PLCs.
cards.trap: Treating OT like a normal laptop domain.

cards.title: Cloud misconfig
cards.secret: Public buckets/over-permissive IAM are top cloud vulns. Scan configs continuously.
cards.trap: Assuming CSP auto-secures your object ACLs.

cards.title: KRI / KPI
cards.secret: KRIs warn rising risk; KPIs measure control/process performance. Both report to leadership.
cards.trap: Using only vanity metrics (ticket count) as risk.

cards.title: Due care vs diligence
cards.secret: Diligence=investigate before deciding; care=ongoing prudent action afterward.

cards.title: SOC 2
cards.secret: Assurance on service org controls vs trust criteria. Read scope/exceptions — logo ≠ coverage.
cards.trap: Accepting any SOC as proof of PCI compliance.

cards.title: Mandatory vacation
cards.secret: Forces another person into the role → can reveal fraud. Pair with SoD.
cards.trap: Calling it only an HR perk.

cards.title: MSSP contracts
cards.secret: Define SLAs, escalation, data handling, logging ownership, exit plan.

cards.title: Data retention
cards.secret: Keep only as long as legal/business need — then securely dispose. Privacy + storage risk.

cards.title: Qualitative vs quantitative
cards.secret: Qual=High/Med/Low scales; Quant=dollars/ALE. Many orgs mix both.
cards.trap: Forcing ALE when no loss data exists.
